passage: Octopuses can change both the color and the texture of their skin in less than a second. This ability allows them to ______ almost perfectly with the rocks, sand, and coral around them. Marine biologist Nodira Usmonova notes that experienced divers often swim within a meter of a resting octopus without noticing it at all.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The text says divers swim right past octopuses “without noticing” them, so the color changes must let octopuses merge visually with their surroundings. “Blend” (to mix in so as to be hard to tell apart) fits.

Choice B is wrong because nothing suggests the octopus is competing with rocks or coral. Choice C is wrong because “collide” means to crash into something, which has nothing to do with camouflage. Choice D is wrong because the octopus is not getting in the way of its surroundings; it is becoming hard to see against them.
explanation_uz:
Matnda g‘avvoslar sakkizoyoqlar yonidan ularni “sezmasdan” o‘tib ketishi aytiladi. Demak, rang o‘zgarishi sakkizoyoqqa atrofidagi narsalar bilan qo‘shilib, ko‘rinmay qolishga imkon beradi. “Blend” (qo‘shilib ketmoq, ajratib bo‘lmas darajada aralashmoq) so‘zi mos keladi.

B noto‘g‘ri: sakkizoyoq tosh yoki marjonlar bilan raqobatlashayotgani haqida gap yo‘q. C noto‘g‘ri: “collide” (to‘qnashmoq) niqoblanishga aloqasi yo‘q. D noto‘g‘ri: sakkizoyoq atrofiga xalaqit bermaydi, aksincha ular fonida ko‘rinmay qoladi.

passage: Before the railway reached it in 1902, the town of Qoraqum was a small and ______ settlement, founded only a few decades earlier. Travelers rarely stopped there, and few people outside the region even knew its name. Within twenty years of the railway's arrival, however, it had become one of the busiest trading centers in the province.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The text says travelers rarely stopped in the town and few outsiders “even knew its name,” so the town was little known. “Obscure” (not well known) fits.

Choice A is wrong because a town that was small and rarely visited was not crowded. Choice B is wrong because the town became a busy trading center only after the railway arrived; before that nothing suggests wealth. Choice D is wrong because the town had been “founded only a few decades earlier,” so it was not ancient.
explanation_uz:
Matnda sayohatchilar bu shaharchada kamdan-kam to‘xtagani va mintaqadan tashqarida uning “nomini ham” kam odam bilgani aytiladi. Demak, shaharcha deyarli noma’lum bo‘lgan. “Obscure” (kam tanilgan, noma’lum) so‘zi mos keladi.

A noto‘g‘ri: kichik va kam qatnaladigan shaharcha gavjum bo‘lmagan. B noto‘g‘ri: shaharcha faqat temir yo‘l kelgandan keyin gavjum savdo markaziga aylangan; undan oldin boylik haqida hech narsa aytilmagan. D noto‘g‘ri: shaharcha “bor-yo‘g‘i bir necha o‘n yil oldin” tashkil topgan, demak u qadimiy emas.

passage: In a survey of 1,200 bus riders, economist Farid Rahimov found that most respondents were ______ to pay a slightly higher fare in exchange for faster service: nearly 70 percent said they would accept a fare increase if it cut their daily travel time by ten minutes.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The colon introduces evidence: nearly 70 percent said they “would accept” a higher fare. So most riders were ready to pay more. “Willing” fits.

Choice A is wrong because “reluctant” (unwilling) is the opposite of what the survey found. Choice B is wrong because the survey asked what riders would accept, not whether they could afford it. Choice C is wrong because nothing in the text says anyone was prohibited from paying.
explanation_uz:
Ikki nuqtadan keyin dalil keltiriladi: qariyb 70 foiz respondent yo‘l haqi oshishini “qabul qilishini” aytgan. Demak, ko‘pchilik ko‘proq to‘lashga tayyor. “Willing” (rozi, tayyor) so‘zi mos keladi.

A noto‘g‘ri: “reluctant” (istamaydigan) so‘rov natijasiga zid. B noto‘g‘ri: so‘rovda yo‘lovchilar nimani qabul qilishi so‘ralgan, puli yetish-yetmasligi emas. D noto‘g‘ri: matnda hech kimga to‘lash taqiqlangani aytilmagan.

passage:
The following text is from a short story.

Malika had expected the old house to feel gloomy after standing empty for so long. But the morning sun poured through every window, lighting up the yellow walls and the painted ceilings, and the rooms seemed almost ______. Before long she found herself humming as she carried her boxes up the stairs.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
“But” signals a contrast with Malika's expectation that the house would be “gloomy.” Sunlight fills the rooms, and she begins humming, so the rooms seem bright and happy. “Cheerful” fits.

Choice A is wrong because “hostile” (unfriendly) is negative, while the details are pleasant. Choice C is wrong because nothing describes the rooms as small or tight. Choice D is wrong because silence is not the opposite of gloominess, and the sunny details do not point to quiet.
explanation_uz:
“But” (lekin) Malikaning uy “g‘amgin” bo‘ladi degan kutilmasiga qarama-qarshilikni bildiradi. Xonalar quyosh nuriga to‘la, Malika esa xirgoyi qila boshlaydi — demak xonalar yorug‘ va quvnoq ko‘rinadi. “Cheerful” (quvnoq, xushchaqchaq) so‘zi mos keladi.

A noto‘g‘ri: “hostile” (dushmanona) salbiy so‘z, tafsilotlar esa yoqimli. C noto‘g‘ri: xonalar tor ekani haqida hech narsa aytilmagan. D noto‘g‘ri: jimjitlik g‘amginlikning teskarisi emas va quyoshli tafsilotlar sukunatga ishora qilmaydi.

passage: Many desert plants sprout, flower, and die within a few weeks after a rare rainstorm. The shrub studied by botanist Aziz Karimov follows a very different strategy: it is remarkably ______. By counting the growth rings in its woody stems, Karimov estimated that some individuals in his study area are more than 300 years old.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The shrub follows a “different strategy” from plants that die within weeks, and some individuals are more than 300 years old. So the shrub lives a very long time. “Long-lived” fits.

Choice A is wrong because the text gives no information about growth speed; the evidence concerns age. Choice B is wrong because nothing says the shrub is uncommon, and its age does not show rarity. Choice D is wrong because toxicity is never mentioned.
explanation_uz:
Buta bir necha haftada nobud bo‘ladigan o‘simliklardan “boshqacha strategiya”ga ega, ba’zi tuplari esa 300 yildan oshiq yashagan. Demak, buta juda uzoq yashaydi. “Long-lived” (uzoq umr ko‘radigan) so‘zi mos keladi.

A noto‘g‘ri: matnda o‘sish tezligi haqida ma’lumot yo‘q, dalil yosh haqida. B noto‘g‘ri: butaning kam uchrashi aytilmagan, yoshi esa kamyobligini ko‘rsatmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: zaharlilik umuman tilga olinmagan.

passage: Historians once assumed that most merchants on the medieval Silk Road traveled only short distances, carrying goods between neighboring towns before handing them on to other traders. A recently studied collection of merchants' letters, however, seems to ______ this assumption: the letters show that some traders regularly made journeys of several thousand kilometers.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
“However” signals that the letters go against the earlier assumption of short journeys, and the colon gives evidence of very long journeys. So the letters call the assumption into question. “Challenge” fits.

Choice A is wrong because the evidence contradicts the assumption rather than supporting it. Choice C is wrong because the letters say something different from the assumption, not the same thing. Choice D is wrong because the letters directly address how far merchants traveled, so they do not ignore the assumption.
explanation_uz:
“However” (biroq) xatlar avvalgi “qisqa safarlar” haqidagi taxminga zid ekanini bildiradi, ikki nuqtadan keyin esa juda uzoq safarlar haqida dalil keltiriladi. Demak, xatlar bu taxminni shubha ostiga qo‘yadi. “Challenge” (e’tiroz bildirmoq, shubha ostiga olmoq) so‘zi mos keladi.

A noto‘g‘ri: dalil taxminni tasdiqlamaydi, aksincha unga zid. C noto‘g‘ri: xatlar taxmindan boshqacha narsani ko‘rsatadi, uni takrorlamaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: xatlar savdogarlar qancha uzoqqa borganiga bevosita taalluqli, ya’ni taxminni e’tiborsiz qoldirmaydi.

passage: Ecologist Sevara Tursunova predicted that adding nitrogen fertilizer to her test plots would boost the growth of the wild grasses planted there. Instead, the fertilizer appeared to ______ their growth: grasses in fertilized plots were on average 15 percent shorter than those in unfertilized plots, most likely because fast-growing weeds thrived on the extra nitrogen and crowded the grasses out.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
“Instead” signals that the result was the opposite of the prediction that fertilizer would “boost” growth, and the grasses in fertilized plots were shorter. So the fertilizer held back their growth. “Inhibit” (to restrain or slow) fits.

Choice B is wrong because “stimulate” means the same as “boost,” the outcome that did not happen. Choice C is wrong because a fertilizer cannot measure growth; researchers do that. Choice D is wrong because a fertilizer does not predict anything, and the sentence describes an effect on the grasses.
explanation_uz:
“Instead” (aksincha) natija o‘g‘it o‘sishni “kuchaytiradi” degan bashoratga teskari bo‘lganini bildiradi: o‘g‘itlangan maydonlardagi o‘tlar pastroq bo‘lib chiqqan. Demak, o‘g‘it o‘sishni to‘xtatib qo‘ygan. “Inhibit” (sekinlashtirmoq, to‘sqinlik qilmoq) so‘zi mos keladi.

B noto‘g‘ri: “stimulate” (rag‘batlantirmoq) aynan “boost” ma’nosini beradi — bu esa ro‘y bermagan natija. C noto‘g‘ri: o‘g‘it o‘sishni o‘lchay olmaydi, buni tadqiqotchilar qiladi. D noto‘g‘ri: o‘g‘it hech narsani bashorat qilmaydi; gap uning o‘tlarga ta’siri haqida.

passage: Sociologist Javlon Rashidov argues that the rapid spread of community gardens in Central Asian cities over the past decade cannot be traced to any one cause. Instead, he contends, it reflects a ______ of several developments, including rising food prices, growing public interest in healthy eating, and city residents' desire for shared green spaces.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
Rashidov says the trend has no single cause and lists several developments that together produced it. A “confluence” is a coming together of several things, which fits “a ______ of several developments.”

Choice A is wrong because the developments are not in conflict with one another; they combine. Choice B is wrong because the text lists several developments, so there is no shortage of them. Choice C is wrong because the text does not rank the causes; it presents them as joint contributors.
explanation_uz:
Rashidov bu tendensiyaning yagona sababi yo‘qligini aytib, uni birgalikda yuzaga keltirgan bir nechta omilni sanab o‘tadi. “Confluence” — bir nechta narsaning bir joyga kelib qo‘shilishi; bu “a ______ of several developments” iborasiga mos keladi.

A noto‘g‘ri: omillar bir-biri bilan nizolashmaydi, aksincha birlashadi. B noto‘g‘ri: matnda bir nechta omil sanalgan, ya’ni ularning tanqisligi yo‘q. C noto‘g‘ri: matn sabablarni darajalarga ajratmaydi, ularni teng hissa qo‘shuvchilar sifatida ko‘rsatadi.

passage:
The following text is from a short story.

Bahrom was no orator. He stammered, lost his place in his notes, and twice apologized to the audience for taking up their time. Yet his plain account of the night the river rose, and of the neighbors he had pulled from the water, carried the meeting, and when the vote was finally taken, nearly every hand in the hall went up in favor of rebuilding the dam.
stem: As used in the text, what does the word “carried” most nearly mean?
explanation_en:
Although Bahrom was a poor speaker, his account led “nearly every hand in the hall” to vote for rebuilding the dam. His speech persuaded the people at the meeting, so “carried” most nearly means “won over.”

Choice A is wrong because Bahrom did not physically move the meeting from one place to another. Choice B is wrong because nothing was raised up by his account; the hands went up because people were persuaded. Choice D is wrong because the account did not make the meeting last longer; it convinced the audience.
explanation_uz:
Bahrom yaxshi notiq bo‘lmasa-da, uning hikoyasi “zaldagi deyarli barcha qo‘llar” to‘g‘onni qayta qurish uchun ko‘tarilishiga olib keldi. Uning nutqi yig‘ilishdagilarni ishontirdi, shuning uchun “carried” bu yerda “won over” (o‘z tomoniga og‘dirdi, ishontirdi) ma’nosini beradi.

A noto‘g‘ri: Bahrom yig‘ilishni bir joydan boshqa joyga ko‘chirmagan. B noto‘g‘ri: hikoya hech narsani yuqoriga ko‘tarmagan; qo‘llar odamlar ishonch hosil qilgani uchun ko‘tarildi. D noto‘g‘ri: hikoya yig‘ilishni cho‘zmagan, tinglovchilarni ishontirgan.

passage: Because the fossil record of the earliest birds is so ______, paleontologists must often reconstruct whole branches of the bird family tree from a few partial skeletons, sometimes from a single incomplete wing or a handful of scattered bones.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
Paleontologists must work from “a few partial skeletons” and even “a single incomplete wing,” which shows that the record is incomplete and broken into pieces. “Fragmentary” (made up of fragments; incomplete) fits.

Choice B is wrong because an abundant record would not force scientists to rely on a few partial skeletons. Choice C is wrong because a disputed record would not explain why so few bones are available. Choice D is wrong because the age of the record has nothing to do with scientists having so little material.
explanation_uz:
Paleontologlar “bir nechta to‘liq bo‘lmagan skelet” va hatto “bitta yarim-yorti qanot” bilan ishlashga majbur — bu qoldiqlar to‘liq emas, parcha-parcha ekanini ko‘rsatadi. “Fragmentary” (parchalardan iborat, to‘liq bo‘lmagan) so‘zi mos keladi.

B noto‘g‘ri: qoldiqlar mo‘l bo‘lsa, olimlar bir nechta parcha bilan cheklanib qolmas edi. C noto‘g‘ri: qoldiqlarning bahsli bo‘lishi suyaklar nega bunchalik kamligini tushuntirmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: qoldiqlarning yoshi materialning ozligiga aloqador emas.

passage: Historian Kamola Yusupova cautions against treating the travel journal of seventeenth-century merchant Ilyos Barlos as a ______ account of the routes he followed. Barlos, she notes, wrote many entries years after the journeys they describe, and several of the dates he gives conflict with customs records kept at the same ports.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
Yusupova points out two problems: entries were written years later, and dates conflict with customs records. Both reasons show that the journal cannot be fully trusted. She therefore cautions against treating it as a “dependable” (reliable) account.

Choice A is wrong because the problems she lists concern accuracy, not whether Barlos was frank or honest about his feelings. Choice B is wrong because a journal based on personal stories is anecdotal, and Yusupova's reasons are not about that. Choice C is wrong because the length of the journal is never discussed.
explanation_uz:
Yusupova ikki muammoni ko‘rsatadi: yozuvlar safardan yillar o‘tib yozilgan va sanalar bojxona hujjatlariga zid. Ikkalasi ham kundalikka to‘liq ishonib bo‘lmasligini bildiradi. Shuning uchun u uni “dependable” (ishonchli) manba deb hisoblamaslikni maslahat beradi.

A noto‘g‘ri: u sanagan muammolar aniqlik haqida, Barlosning samimiyligi haqida emas. B noto‘g‘ri: “anecdotal” (shaxsiy hikoyalarga asoslangan) degan ma’no Yusupovaning dalillariga mos kelmaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: kundalikning hajmi umuman muhokama qilinmaydi.

passage: When an earthquake occurs, its seismic waves reach different monitoring stations at slightly different times. By comparing these arrival times across several stations, seismologists can now ______ the point where the earthquake began to within a few hundred meters, often in less than a minute.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The text describes locating an earthquake's origin “to within a few hundred meters,” which means identifying it very precisely. “Pinpoint” (to locate exactly) fits.

Choice A is wrong because the method uses waves that have already arrived, so it locates an earthquake after it begins rather than anticipating (expecting) it. Choice C is wrong because the method reveals the location; it does not hide it. Choice D is wrong because nothing suggests exaggerating or making the location seem more exciting.
explanation_uz:
Matnda zilzila boshlangan nuqtani “bir necha yuz metr aniqlikda” topish tasvirlangan, ya’ni joy juda aniq belgilanadi. “Pinpoint” (aniq belgilamoq) so‘zi mos keladi.

A noto‘g‘ri: usul allaqachon yetib kelgan to‘lqinlardan foydalanadi, ya’ni zilzilani oldindan kutmaydi (“anticipate”), balki boshlangandan keyin uning joyini aniqlaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: usul joyni yashirmaydi, aksincha ochib beradi. D noto‘g‘ri: joyni bo‘rttirib ko‘rsatish haqida gap yo‘q.

passage: Early naturalists described the nest building of potter wasps as almost mechanical, assuming that each wasp simply ran through a fixed series of steps. Yet when entomologist Rano Abdullayeva damaged half-built nests, the wasps did not start the series over from the beginning; they repaired only the damaged section and then altered the shape of the next cells to compensate. Such behavior suggests that the wasps' building is far less ______ than early accounts implied.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
Early naturalists thought the wasps followed “a fixed series of steps.” Abdullayeva found that the wasps changed what they did in response to damage. So the building is less fixed or unchanging than the early accounts said. “Invariable” (never changing) fits.

Choice A is the reverse trap: the wasps' repairs show that the behavior is more adaptive, not less. Choice B is wrong because the early accounts called the behavior “mechanical,” not complex, and the new evidence does not show it is simpler. Choice D is wrong because the text does not discuss how much effort the building requires.
explanation_uz:
Ilk tabiatshunoslar arilar “qat’iy bir qator bosqichlar”ga amal qiladi deb o‘ylashgan. Abdullayeva esa arilar shikastga qarab xatti-harakatini o‘zgartirishini aniqladi. Demak, uya qurish avvalgi ta’riflardagidan ancha kamroq qat’iy, o‘zgarmas. “Invariable” (o‘zgarmas) so‘zi mos keladi.

A — teskari tuzoq: tuzatishlar xatti-harakat kamroq emas, balki ko‘proq moslashuvchan (“adaptive”) ekanini ko‘rsatadi. B noto‘g‘ri: ilk ta’riflarda xatti-harakat murakkab emas, “mexanik” deyilgan va yangi dalil uni soddaroq deb ko‘rsatmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: matnda qurilish qancha mehnat talab qilishi muhokama qilinmaydi.

passage: Critics long dismissed the late canvases of painter Ozod Mirzayev as ______, pointing to their thin layers of paint and loose, rapid brushwork as signs that the aging artist no longer took much trouble over his work. A recent technical study, however, found detailed preparatory drawings beneath nearly every one of these canvases, suggesting that their apparent spontaneity was carefully planned.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The critics saw the late paintings as signs that the artist “no longer took much trouble over his work.” “Perfunctory” means done with little care or effort, merely to get it done, which matches the critics' dismissal.

Choice A is wrong because “meticulous” (extremely careful) describes what the technical study revealed, not what the critics claimed; it reverses the charge. Choice C is wrong because “ponderous” means heavy and slow, the opposite of “loose, rapid brushwork.” Choice D is wrong because “derivative” means copied from others, and the critics' complaint is about lack of effort, not lack of originality.
explanation_uz:
Tanqidchilar kechki rasmlarni rassom “endi ishiga unchalik e’tibor bermay qo‘ygani”ning belgisi deb bilishgan. “Perfunctory” — shunchaki qutulish uchun, yuzaki va kam e’tibor bilan qilingan degani; bu tanqidchilarning fikriga to‘liq mos keladi.

A noto‘g‘ri: “meticulous” (o‘ta sinchkov) texnik tadqiqot aniqlagan narsani ifodalaydi, tanqidchilarning da’vosini emas — ma’no teskari. C noto‘g‘ri: “ponderous” (og‘ir, sust) “erkin, tez mo‘yqalam harakatlari”ga zid. D noto‘g‘ri: “derivative” (boshqalardan ko‘chirilgan) originallik yo‘qligini bildiradi, tanqidchilar esa mehnat yetishmasligidan shikoyat qilgan.

passage: Anthropologist Laylo Hamidova spent a year studying vendors in a large bazaar, where sellers of the same goods almost never undercut one another's prices. No vendor she interviewed could say when the practice began or who had first proposed it, and none had ever discussed it openly with competitors. Yet violations were rare and were swiftly punished, usually by the offender's neighbors refusing to trade with him. The arrangement, in other words, is ______ but firmly enforced.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The vendors' agreement was never proposed by anyone known and never “discussed … openly,” yet everyone follows it. “Tacit” means understood without being stated, which fits. The word “but” contrasts this unspoken quality with the firm enforcement.

Choice B is wrong because nothing suggests the arrangement is temporary; no one remembers when it began. Choice C is wrong because a contentious arrangement would be disputed, yet the text says no one discusses it and violations are rare. Choice D is the reverse trap: “codified” means written down as formal rules, the opposite of an agreement that was never stated.
explanation_uz:
Sotuvchilarning kelishuvini kim taklif qilgani noma’lum va u hech qachon “ochiq muhokama qilinmagan”, lekin hamma unga amal qiladi. “Tacit” — aytilmasa ham tushuniladigan, so‘zsiz degani; bu mos keladi. “But” (lekin) shu so‘zsizlikni qattiq nazorat bilan qarama-qarshi qo‘yadi.

B noto‘g‘ri: kelishuv vaqtinchalik (“provisional”) ekaniga hech qanday ishora yo‘q; uning qachon boshlanganini hech kim eslamaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: “contentious” (bahsli) kelishuv tortishuvlarga sabab bo‘lardi, matnda esa uni hech kim muhokama qilmaydi va buzilishlar kam. D — teskari tuzoq: “codified” (rasmiy qoidalar sifatida yozib qo‘yilgan) hech qachon aytilmagan kelishuvning aksi.

passage: For decades, astronomers assumed that the bright spot near the south pole of an icy moon orbiting a distant planet was a lasting surface feature, perhaps a field of fresh frost. But images collected since 1990 by planetary scientist Timur Ganiyev's team tell a different story. Rather than a constant presence, the spot is ______: it has faded from view and then reappeared at least four times, each time remaining visible for a year or more.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
“Rather than a constant presence” and the colon's explanation (the spot fades and reappears “at least four times”) show that the spot comes and goes repeatedly. “Intermittent” (stopping and starting at intervals) fits.

Choice A is wrong because “ephemeral” means lasting only a very short time; it says nothing about returning, and each appearance lasts “a year or more.” Choice B is wrong because “immutable” (unchanging) fits the old view of a lasting feature, which the new images contradict. Choice C is wrong because “incipient” means just beginning to appear, but the spot has been observed repeatedly over decades.
explanation_uz:
“Rather than a constant presence” (doimiy mavjud bo‘lish o‘rniga) iborasi va ikki nuqtadan keyingi izoh (dog‘ “kamida to‘rt marta” yo‘qolib, yana paydo bo‘lgan) dog‘ vaqti-vaqti bilan paydo bo‘lib, yo‘qolib turishini ko‘rsatadi. “Intermittent” (uzilib-uzilib, oraliqlar bilan takrorlanadigan) so‘zi mos keladi.

A noto‘g‘ri: “ephemeral” juda qisqa muddat davom etadigan degani va qayta paydo bo‘lishni bildirmaydi; bundan tashqari, har safar dog‘ “bir yil yoki undan ko‘proq” ko‘rinib turgan. B noto‘g‘ri: “immutable” (o‘zgarmas) yangi tasvirlar rad etgan eski “doimiy belgi” qarashiga mos. C noto‘g‘ri: “incipient” endigina paydo bo‘layotgan degani, dog‘ esa o‘n yillar davomida qayta-qayta kuzatilgan.
